xBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-5452: Computer use: let agents drive local desktop apps with `pan computer` (Linux, vendored Orca helper)

plan.title: Computer use: let agents drive local desktop apps with `pan computer` (Linux, vendored Orca helper)
plan.author: agent:claude-opus-5-5

narratives.Problem: Overdeck agents cannot see or operate desktop apps. Orca's MIT-licensed Linux computer-use helper (one Python file reading AT-SPI, taking screenshots and sending xdotool/XTest input) runs standalone, but Overdeck has no way to call it, no guard against two agents driving the one shared pointer and keyboard, no way to find the desktop session env from agent shells that lack DISPLAY, and no opt-in switch.
narratives.Proposal: Vendor the helper verbatim at native/computer-use-linux/runtime.py pinned to Orca c6b9ac9549b with a port record; add src/lib/computer-use/ (paths, errors, desktop env resolution via systemctl --user show-environment, a helper runner with private 0600 operation files, a file lock plus a 120 s renewable desktop lease, a per-holder snapshot cache, the ported Linux blocked-shortcut list, a tree filter, text/JSON formatting, a guarded run preamble, per-command operation builders and a fake-timer-tested wait); expose it as the pan computer CLI verb with 15 subcommands; gate everything except capabilities and release behind global-only computer_use.enabled; ship a pan-computer-use skill, a pan doctor row, docs and a changelog entry; verify live on the operator's X11 desktop.
narratives.NonGoals:
- macOS (signed Swift helper) and Windows (runtime.ps1) support; both refuse with unsupported_platform
- MCP tools for computer use in the overdeck MCP server
- Any dashboard route, Settings toggle, lease display or live view (no new HTTP route, no no-loss-matrix row)
- Tree diffs, suspected-noop verification and Orca's agent-facing error-code mapping (helper errors pass through as helper_error)
- Any local edit to the vendored runtime.py beyond the two port header lines
- Setting computer_use from a project .pan.yaml (the project layer is stripped)
- Turning computer_use on in the operator's real ~/.overdeck/config.yaml during implementation or verification
- Wayland hotkey support beyond what the helper reports
- Remote-host or Fly detection logic beyond refusing when no display resolves
- Shipping the helper inside the Electron desktop app bundle
- New npm or Python dependencies
- Raising any scripts/file-size-allowlist.txt cap

metadata.sizeJustification: One opt-in feature defined as a single deliverable by the issue body. About 40 files across many top-level paths, but the logic lives in one new directory (src/lib/computer-use/, 12 modules each with its own test); the rest are mandatory one-to-five-line touchpoints of adding a CLI verb and config key (command-groups, index, curation, generated manifest, umbrella skill, skill fixture, docs nav, changelog, CLI reference, port records, package files). Splitting would ship a verb without its gate, skill or docs. The plan is decomposed into 18 items with a parallel-friendly DAG instead.

autoDecisions.summary: Kept the PRD's single-issue scope and set plan.metadata.sizeJustification instead of splitting into sibling issues.
autoDecisions.rationale: The issue body defines one opt-in feature; the wide surface is mandatory per-verb touchpoints (docs nav, changelog, skill fixture, curation, generated manifest), while the logic lives in one new directory, and a verb without its config gate, skill or docs would ship a half feature.

autoDecisions.summary: Defined pan computer capabilities as never refusing (new FR-13) and release as lease-only under the lock.
autoDecisions.rationale: The PRD exempted capabilities from the config gate but left the platform and desktop checks ambiguous; a readiness query that refuses is useless, and an operator must always be able to clear a stuck lease.

autoDecisions.summary: Split the command layer into run.ts (preamble), commands.ts and wait.ts, and pulled paths.ts plus errors.ts into a foundation item.
autoDecisions.rationale: Lets the library modules run in parallel, keeps every file far under the 1,000-line ceiling, and gives the security-relevant preamble its own reviewed commit.

autoDecisions.summary: Helper calls use killSignal SIGKILL and treat execFile killed === true as helper_timeout.
autoDecisions.rationale: The vendored helper traps SIGTERM, and a hung AT-SPI D-Bus call never reaches a Python signal handler.

autoDecisions.summary: Added the umbrella pan skill line, the computer Core curation category, a cli/core-commands.mdx section and tests/unit/cli placement.
autoDecisions.rationale: These are the files the semgrep verb precedent (PAN-4585, PAN-4592) touched that the draft omitted.

autoDecisions.summary: Kept the skill name pan-computer-use and replaced the lint:skills coverage it misses with an explicit loop over its commands.
autoDecisions.rationale: The issue body names the skill; lint-skills.sh only validates pan-<verb> skills, so the loop is the only check that the skill's flags exist.

autoDecisions.summary: Live verification runs the workspace build in a throwaway home at a literal path under ~/.overdeck/tmp.
autoDecisions.rationale: The global pan is the deployed build without the feature, the operator's real config must never be switched on by an agent, and rm targets must be literal paths.

narrative.Action: Follow PRD 3h (run.ts part): create src/lib/computer-use/run.ts exporting runComputerOperation({ kind: 'read' | 'input', operation, deps }) that runs, in order: platform check (non-linux -> unsupported_platform), config check (computerUse.enabled false -> disabled), resolveDesktopEnv (failure -> no_desktop_session), then withDesktopLock around claimLease (input only) + runHelper(operation, { env }) + saveSnapshot + saveScreenshot. Also export runCapabilities() per FR-13 (never refuses; handshake only on linux with a desktop env, under the lock, no lease; helper failure fills helperError) and runRelease({ force }) (releaseLease inside withDesktopLock only). All side effects come through injectable deps with real defaults. Add __tests__/run.test.ts.
